title: Microsoft 365 & Azure status
summary: Microsoft's public status: Azure, the Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft 365 consumer services and Azure incidents.
description:
Reads Microsoft's public status pages (status.cloud.microsoft and azure.status.microsoft) - no account or credential needed.

"Azure - status" and "Microsoft 365 - status" are Microsoft's overall verdicts; "Microsoft 365 consumer services" gives every consumer service (Outlook.com, OneDrive, Teams free ...) its own channel; "Azure - incidents (RSS)" counts open Azure incidents.

Note: the health of YOUR tenant's Exchange Online, Teams or SharePoint is only in the Microsoft 365 admin center (Service health) and needs a sign-in to Microsoft Graph; these templates show what Microsoft reports publicly - which is what matters when a whole region is down.
tags: Status page, Microsoft 365, Azure, Exchange Online, Microsoft
author: Matmon.eu

title: AWS status
summary: Amazon Web Services' public health feed: open events of every service and region.
description:
Reads the public AWS Health Dashboard feed - no AWS account needed.

"AWS - service health (RSS)" counts open AWS events (an item closes when AWS marks it resolved). The default feed covers every service in every region; to watch only what you use, change the sensor's target to that service's feed, e.g. https://status.aws.amazon.com/rss/ec2-eu-central-1.rss (the dashboard lists every feed).
author: Matmon.eu

title: Google Cloud & Google Workspace status
summary: Google's public incident feeds for Google Cloud and Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Meet ...).
description:
Reads Google's public status dashboards - no account needed.

"Google Cloud - incidents (Atom)" and "Google Workspace - incidents (Atom)" count open incidents; an incident closes when Google marks it RESOLVED.
tags: Status page, Google Cloud, Google Workspace, Gmail, Google
author: Matmon.eu

title: Hornetsecurity status
summary: Hornetsecurity's public status page: every service, every service per location, and open incidents and maintenance.
description:
Reads Hornetsecurity's public status page (status.io API and its RSS feed) - no account or credential needed.

"Hornetsecurity - services" gives every service (Spam and Malware Protection, Email Encryption, Backup ...) its own channel; "Hornetsecurity - services by location" does the same per data centre ("Spam and Malware Protection - Germany - Frankfurt"); "Hornetsecurity - incidents (RSS)" counts open incidents and maintenance. A service that is not operational turns its channel - and the sensor - to warning or error, and the message names it.
tags: Status page, Hornetsecurity, E-mail security, Microsoft 365
author: Matmon.eu

title: GitHub status
summary: GitHub's public status: overall, every component (Git, Actions, Copilot ...) and incidents.
description:
Reads GitHub's public status page (www.githubstatus.com) - no account or credential needed.

"GitHub - overall status" is the page's own verdict (All Systems Operational / Minor / Major Outage / Maintenance) as one channel; "GitHub - components" gives every component its own channel, so a warning names what is affected; "GitHub - incidents (RSS)" counts open incidents and maintenance from the page's history feed.

Add the templates to a host or folder of your choice and create a sensor from each; the target is already set.
author: Matmon.eu

title: Slack status

"Slack - status" is Slack's overall verdict plus the number of active incidents (a warning from the first one); "Slack - incidents (RSS)" counts open incidents and maintenance.
